period.interpretation: The dataset is exactly 672 UTC hours. The local calendar month-slice 1-28 Oct is 673 elapsed hours because 25 Oct has 25 hours; the dataset covers 671 of them plus 00:00 on 29 Oct local, and lacks 00:00-01:59 on 1 Oct local. Anything keyed on naive local time sees only 671 distinct wall-clock hours and silently merges the two 02:00 hours. Rule: compute elapsed time, joins and totals in UTC; use local time only for labels and hour-of-day patterns; per-day comparisons must normalise by hours present (25 Oct = 25 h).

valuation.price_component: synthetic spot energy only, excl. VAT, network fees, energy tax, markup and fixed fees
valuation.carbon_factor_type: synthetic operational average factor (not marginal, not lifecycle)

tariff_rules.monthly_average_spot: reductions approx. value_spot_timeavg_sek; load shifting 0 SEK
tariff_rules.fixed_price: reductions = kWh x user's contract price; load shifting 0 SEK
tariff_rules.included_in_rent: 0 SEK to the student; kWh and CO2e still change

missing_vs_zero.principle: A missing observation (empty, N/A, negative, spike or absent record) means the energy is UNKNOWN, not zero. A measured 0.0 means the channel was observed off. The analytical table keeps both apart: energy_status/energy_missing flags; cost and CO2e stay missing when kWh or price is missing.
missing_vs_zero.central_method: same channel's mean at the same local hour of day (estimate only; no rows are imputed)
missing_vs_zero.upper_method: same channel's maximum observed hourly value
missing_vs_zero.example_vacancy_is_measured_low_energy: F003 13-15 Oct: occupants 0, observed 2.18 kWh/day - real low use, not missing data

A01.reasoning: Continuous, never-zero ~50 W load with no daily or weather cycle in 7 flats is the classic cold-appliance signature; hourly data cannot show compressor cycling, so a different always-on device cannot be excluded.

A02.reasoning: Large (~0.8 kWh) one-hour events at breakfast, lunch and dinner, more at weekends; matches cooking. Kettle/microwave clusters would be smaller.

A03.reasoning: Isolated ~0.67 kWh one-hour events every ~2-3 days at varied daytime hours. Consistent with a washing machine but also with a tumble dryer on eco or other occasional appliance.

A04.reasoning: ~0.9 kWh events every 2 days at exactly 20:00 in all flats: a cycle-type appliance on a fixed habit/timer. Size fits a dishwasher eco cycle; a dryer would usually use more.

A05.reasoning: 4 W standby 08-17 h, a flat-specific constant 53-89 W 21-08 h scaling with resident count, ~30-50 W 17-21 h. Plausibly personal electronics/chargers, but the night level is too high for phone charging alone.

A06.reasoning: 33 W constant floor plus an evening (17-23 h) increase of 27-55 W; evening shape fits lighting/TV. The floor could be a router or standby loads.

A07.reasoning: Used by 2 flats only; hourly energy = 0.12 kWh/h per degC below 12 degC (residual sd 0.003 kWh); README states portable heaters are the supplementary electric heat in scope.

opportunities.title: F007: portable heater runs while the flat is unoccupied

observed_evidence.heater_model_check: hourly kWh = 0.12 x (12.0 - outdoor degC), residual sd 0.003 kWh - heater output depends on weather only, not on presence
observed_evidence.denominator_note: Each count names its base. 'Unoccupied' = occupants_home == 0 among hours with known occupancy; hours with unknown occupancy are never counted as unoccupied; a missing heater reading is never counted as 'off'. F007: 64 unoccupied, 56 with heater on (= 55 cold hours with known outdoor temperature + 1 hour with unknown outdoor temperature); the 8 others were >= 12 degC so the weather-driven heater was off anyway. F001: 142 unoccupied, 141 with a valid heater reading, all 0 kWh; of the 124 cold ones, 123 have a valid reading.

comparator_F001.note: F001's heater is off in every unoccupied hour and on whenever occupied and <12 degC

demonstrated: The heater delivered 23.27 kWh in 56 hours that the occupancy estimate marks as empty.
F001 never heats an empty flat: 0 kWh in all 141 unoccupied hours with a valid heater reading (142 unoccupied, 1 reading missing).
Heater output follows outdoor temperature only (r = -1.00), so it is not switched by anyone in F007.
hypotheses: That the occupancy estimate is correct for every hour (it is a simulated sensor; 42 of 52 episodes last only 1 h, which could partly be sensor noise).
That heating during absence is not needed for comfort on return (indoor temperature stays 22.5 degC either way in the data, so no comfort effect is measurable).
That no re-heating rebound occurs after the heater is switched back on (not observable: heater output is weather-determined).

intervention.action: Switch the portable heater off when leaving for 2 h or more; optionally automate with a timer/presence control.

safety: Portable heaters should not be left running unattended; switching off when leaving also reduces fire risk.
Peak observed draw 1.23 kWh in an hour (>=1.2 kW): any smart/timer plug must be rated for the heater's nameplate load, and the heater's manual must permit use with timers.
comfort: F007's indoor temperature is 22.5 degC whether the heater is on or off (other flats 20.5 degC with district heating only), so the data give no sign that switching off during absences makes the flat cold - but the heater's effect on indoor temperature cannot be measured here.
equipment_control: Manual switching is realistic only for longer absences; 1-h gaps need automation.

measured_inputs: hourly spot price and carbon factor
assumptions: heater is off (0 kWh) in the selected unoccupied hours
no re-heating rebound in the central case
consumption in occupied hours is unchanged
same weather and prices as observed
counterfactual.formula: savings_kWh = sum over selected unoccupied hours h of A07_kWh(h); SEK_hourly = sum A07_kWh(h) x spot(h); CO2e = sum A07_kWh(h) x carbon(h)/1000

opportunities.title: F005: persistent ~95 W elevated base consumption

context.note: Peers with 2-4 residents and 56-82 m2 all share an identical 33 W floor, so size does not explain a constant +95 W.

demonstrated: A constant additive +95 W on A06 in every one of 661 valid hours for 4 weeks, including unoccupied and overnight hours.
Evening use above the floor (+70 W) is in the normal range of other flats, so the anomaly is a fixed always-on device, not more active use.
hypotheses: Which device it is (light left on, TV/console standby, aquarium/terrarium, network storage, or a building load wired to the flat's circuit).
Whether it is avoidable - some always-on devices are needed.

intervention.action: Locate the always-on device (check lights/LED strips, TV/console/speaker standby, chargers, aquariums) and switch it off or put it on a switched power strip/timer.
intervention.who: student first; housing provider if the load turns out to be fixed installation

safety: Do not switch off devices that must run continuously (e.g. medical equipment, aquarium life support).
comfort: None expected if it is an unused light or standby load.
equipment_control: Hourly data cannot identify the device; finding it needs a walk-round or a plug-in power meter.

measured_inputs: A06 minimum of the 7 other flats (33 W)
assumptions: a fraction f of the 95 W excess is removed in every hour (f = 1, 0.5, 0.25)
evening use above the floor unchanged
no hour falls below the peer floor

scenarios.label: Excess base load fully eliminated (device found and switched off)
scenarios.tariff_applicability: kWh and CO2e change on any tariff. SEK: hourly spot contract -> value_spot_hourly_sek; monthly-average spot -> approx. value_spot_timeavg_sek; fixed price -> kWh x own price; electricity included in rent -> 0 SEK to the student.

scenarios.label: Half of the excess avoidable (e.g. device needed part-time or replaced by a lower-power one)

scenarios.label: Quarter of the excess avoidable

uncertainty.note: Measurement uncertainty is negligible (constant load); savings range is driven by f. f = 0.5 is a neutral midpoint chosen because nothing in the data indicates how much of the load is avoidable - it is not an estimate. Because the load is flat across all hours, hourly-spot and time-average values are nearly equal.

rate_if_persistent.note: A constant load would continue at this rate; any longer-period figure is an extrapolation and depends on that period's prices.

steps: switch off one candidate at a time and check next-day data

opportunities.statistical_confidence: very high that the +95 W always-on load exists
opportunities.action_feasibility: medium: depends on finding the device

must_confirm: What is always on in the flat?

opportunities.title: F002: sudden, sustained x2.4 increase in refrigerator-like consumption

data_quality_flags.artefact_checks: step is abrupt (one hour), confined to this channel; other F002 channels, occupancy, indoor temperature and the other 7 fridges show no change; values after the step are realistic noise, not a constant or unit artefact

demonstrated: Mean consumption rose from 0.0517 to 0.122 kWh/h (x2.36) between 2026-10-15T01:00:00+02:00 and 2026-10-15T02:00:00+02:00, and stayed there for all 14 remaining days with no recovery trend.
No simultaneous change in occupancy, indoor temperature, other F002 channels or other flats' fridges.
hypotheses: Cause: fault (door seal, thermostat, defrost, fan, compressor) vs a user setting (fast-freeze/super-cool left on, door not closing, fridge overfilled after shopping) vs a second appliance added to the circuit.
That a repair returns consumption to the pre-step level.

intervention.action: Student checks first: door closes and seals, fast-freeze/super-cool mode off, thermostat at normal setting (about 4 degC fridge / -18 degC freezer), vents not blocked, no heavy frost. If unchanged, report to the housing provider.

safety: Never switch the fridge off to 'save' energy: food safety comes first.
equipment_control: Appliances in student housing are often provider-owned; repairs typically need the provider (assumption: ownership not in data).

measured_inputs: hourly A01 kWh (F002) before and after the step
assumptions: after repair, consumption returns to the pre-step mean (central) or peer mean (sensitivity)
repair at the moment of the step (retrospective) - real savings start only when it is actually fixed
counterfactual.formula: savings_kWh = sum over post-step hours h of max(0, A01(h) - pre_mean); savings rate = (post_mean - pre_mean) per hour

scenarios.label: Repaired at the step: excess over the pre-step mean avoided for the 14 observed post-step days (retrospective)
scenarios.tariff_applicability: kWh and CO2e change on any tariff. SEK: hourly spot contract -> value_spot_hourly_sek; monthly-average spot -> approx. value_spot_timeavg_sek; fixed price -> kWh x own price; electricity included in rent -> 0 SEK to the student.

scenarios.label: Repaired to the peer-fridge mean (0.0526 kWh/h) instead of F002's own pre-step mean
scenarios.tariff_applicability: kWh and CO2e change on any tariff. SEK: hourly spot contract -> value_spot_hourly_sek; monthly-average spot -> approx. value_spot_timeavg_sek; fixed price -> kWh x own price; electricity included in rent -> 0 SEK to the student.

scenarios.label: Partial fix (e.g. door/seal adjusted, compressor still degraded): half the excess avoided
scenarios.tariff_applicability: kWh and CO2e change on any tariff. SEK: hourly spot contract -> value_spot_hourly_sek; monthly-average spot -> approx. value_spot_timeavg_sek; fixed price -> kWh x own price; electricity included in rent -> 0 SEK to the student.

savings_rate_while_unrepaired.reconciliation: central kWh = excess rate x observed post-step hours = 0.07037 x 332 = 23.36; window has 336 h, 4 missing
savings_rate_while_unrepaired.note: Each day of delay costs this much energy. Future prices differ; this is a rate, not a forecast.

uncertainty.statistical: the excess rate itself is very precisely measured (Welch t ~ 90)

actionability.actor: student checks settings/door; housing provider repairs
steps: if no change in 24-48 h, report fault with the step date as evidence

opportunities.statistical_confidence: very high that the step is real
opportunities.action_feasibility: medium: student can check settings; repair depends on the provider

must_confirm: Did anything change on 15 October (new appliance, fast-freeze, door problem)?
must_not_say: That the fridge is definitely broken.

opportunities.title: F004: electronics-like load stays on during the day

observed_evidence.other_hours_vs_2_resident_peers: 21-08 h identical to F001/F008 (0.053 kWh/h); 17-20 h within 0.01 kWh/h; only 09-16 h differs

demonstrated: A 69 W load runs from 09:00 to 16:59 local on every day, independent of whether anyone is home; every other flat is at 4 W in those hours.
Outside 09-17 h F004 matches the other 2-resident flats exactly.
hypotheses: The rigid 09:00-17:00 block suggests a timer/schedule (e.g. a PC, console or display on a schedule, or a device on a timer plug) rather than forgetfulness.
Whether the device is doing useful work (e.g. a computation/download) - if so it is not waste.

intervention.action: Identify what runs 09:00-17:00 (check device schedules, timer plugs, PC sleep settings) and switch it off or enable sleep when not in use.

equipment_control: If the device performs needed work, shift or shorten rather than remove.

measured_inputs: median A05 of the other 7 flats by local hour
assumptions: daytime consumption falls to the peer median for the same hour (4 W)
counterfactual.formula: savings_kWh = sum over 09-16 h of max(0, A05_F004(h) - peer_median(local_hour(h)))

opportunities.title: Dishwasher always starts at 20:00, inside the evening price peak (all flats)

observed_evidence.cadence: every 2 days in each flat (gaps of 4-6 days coincide with missing readings or F003's vacancy)

data_quality_flags.note: Two expected runs fall in missing 20:00 readings; they are not counted (savings slightly understated, ~2 x 0.9 kWh).

demonstrated: All 108 observed runs start at exactly 20:00 local, the most expensive hour block of the day (0.92 vs 0.31 SEK/kWh at 21:00).
Moving the same kWh changes cost and CO2e, not consumption.
hypotheses: That the 20:00 start is a habit/timer the student controls.
That the household has an hourly-price contract (otherwise no SEK effect).
That the appliance is a dishwasher (inferred).

intervention.action: Start the dishwasher at 21:00 or later (manually or with delay-start).

safety: Running appliances unattended or overnight is commonly discouraged for fire and water-leak safety; the 21:00 option avoids overnight running.
comfort: Shared-housing quiet hours (often 22:00-07:00) may restrict later starts. The data show each run's energy within one hour; a real cycle started at 21:00 may continue past 22:00.
equipment_control: Overnight options need a delay-start function; price-optimal timing needs day-ahead prices (published the previous afternoon) or an app.

measured_inputs: hourly spot price and carbon factor
assumptions: whole cycle falls in the destination hour
if a destination price is missing the event is not valued
counterfactual.formula: value_SEK = sum_events kWh_e x (spot(h_e) - spot(h_e')); CO2e = sum kWh_e x (carbon(h_e) - carbon(h_e'))/1000; kWh change = 0

rankings.note: Three separate orderings; no composite score. Impact uses each opportunity's CENTRAL scenario over its own stated period (28 days for all except O3: 14 post-step days).
rankings.comparability_note: O3's observed saving covers only the 14 post-step days; at the measured excess rate an unrepaired fault adds 47.29 kWh per 28 days (persistence assumption), which would rank it first on kWh. O2's central value rests on the arbitrary f = 0.5 (range 25-100 %). O5 saves no kWh by design.
